title: Agent course, round one: engine, content, fridges, xAPI, package
description:
Round one of the course: the engine, the eight modules' content, the two fridge activities, the xAPI layer for SparkLMS, the tincan.xml package, and the e2e run that proves it. Built by the workflow it teaches.

POINTERS. PLAN.md §2 (the idea), §3 (how the workflow maps), §4 (constraints), §6 (the decision record, written by bead .1). docs/course/README.md (the course design: audience, the one message, the module shape, the fake agent, assessment, statements, decisions C1-C17 = D1-D17) and docs/course/modules/00..07 (the storyboard: every screen, every interaction's script, every check with feedback), docs/course/glossary.md. docs/design/2026-10-15-first-pass/ (the look: README has the tokens and fonts; one .dc.html per screen, the course's own source of truth for layout and copy where the storyboard and the design differ, the design wins). Bead agent-course-r4n (the brief: its description is the one-screen summary, its notes carry D18-D24 with reasons and the SparkLMS launch findings). docs/conversations/2026-10-15-brief.md.

IN SCOPE. The content schema and YAML loader; the course shell (scenario, home with the box, module frame); every screen type the storyboard uses (scene, takeaway, chat, brief, choose, match, order, fridge, compare); the fridge drag-and-drop in its two configurations; the xAPI layer (TinCan launch, 1.0.2, the Spark auth verbatim, statements D19, State resume D22, preview mode with an in-memory store, a PREVIEW badge and a statements drawer); progress, score and resume; the tincan.xml package build; the e2e tier playing the whole course and a launch URL; the recorded walkthrough.

OUT OF SCOPE (later epics). cmi5 or SCORM; the Spark postMessage bridge, keydown forwarding and a Close button (D23); a pass mark or "passed" unless Spark UAT needs it (D11, D19); anything found on Spark UAT after the first import (new beads under a round-two epic); narration or video (D12); a developer track; translation; changes to any skill.
notes:
**DECISIONS** (epic-scoped log; durable record written to PLAN.md §6 in bead .1)
- D1-D24 bind every bead: D1-D17 are docs/course/README.md §9 (same numbers); D18-D24 are on bead agent-course-r4n's notes with their reasons. The rules below are this epic's own.
- Content is YAML under content/ (course.yaml; modules/00..07.yaml; fridge/one-shot.yaml and fridge/accepted.yaml), parsed at build time by a Vite YAML plugin, validated by one schema at startup and in a unit test, and nothing is fetched at run time (D13, D21, CLAUDE.md). The storyboard in docs/course/modules/ is the source of the copy and the YAML carries it word for word; where the design boards differ from the storyboard, the design wins.
- One schema, one owner: src/content/ is bead .2's. A screen bead that needs a field the schema lacks files a bead here (CHANGE PROTOCOL); it never edits the schema.
- Screen types, fixed by .2 and built by .3-.7: scene (heading, eyebrow, body blocks: paragraph, cards, quote, numbered list, aside with a glossary term), takeaway (the card and the wall gained), chat (a fixed learner opening, agent messages, reply options each with the agent's scripted reply, branches that wander with a debrief, a free-text box echoed back and never judged, a side panel), brief (ranked questions with chips, the recommended one marked, the decision text per option filling a panel, a playback message, round two, a "Your defaults" button, a closing message), choose (prompt, options with label, right-or-wrong and feedback, mode multi or single, scored or not; the checks are scored single-choice), match (rows each with a key among a shared set of targets, feedback per row, scored or not), order (cards in a correct order, keyboard-operable, scored), fridge (one fridge from a fridge file), compare (two fridges side by side and a table of differences). Every interaction and check carries a slug that becomes its activity id (D24).
- The scenario and the home page are course-level pages (the storyboard's module 00 screens 1 and 2); module 00 starts at "The request". The home page always lets a learner open any module (D22).
- The look is the design's first pass: the tokens, type and exclusions in docs/design/2026-10-15-first-pass/README.md; fonts bundled with @fontsource packages imported from src/index.css (precedent in the presentation repo, CLAUDE.md: nothing fetched at run time). Icons are inline SVG; no emoji, no gradient washes, no cream or serif display, no left-border cards.
- Routing is hash-based so the LMS launch query string survives every navigation (D18, D23). Library or hand-rolled is the developer's call.
- Screens are driven by their content and report through one event callback the frame gives them (answered with the option and whether it was right, interacted with the option or branch, fridge ended with its score, takeaway reached). .3 defines the callback, .4-.7 call it, .9 consumes it. No screen talks to the record store.
- Progress and score: a check or capstone item can be re-answered and the latest answer is what counts (as the fridge's D7); a module is complete when its takeaway is reached; the course is complete when all eight are; the score is 30 points (two checks per module at one point each, the capstone's 8 order points and 6 wall points) and the scaled score is points over 30. The course "completed" statement is sent when the last module completes and again with the new score whenever a scored item changes afterwards.
- Resume (D22): progress (modules completed, screen reached, every answer) is written to the State API under the course activity, agent and registration after every change, and to localStorage always; on load, State wins when it exists, else localStorage. In preview there is no State API, so localStorage carries it.
- Preview mode (D18): no endpoint in the URL means an in-memory record store, a PREVIEW badge in the top bar, and a statements drawer (newest first, verb and object and result) a designer or a test can read. With an endpoint there is no badge and no drawer.
- Statements (D19, D23, D24): actor verbatim from the launch; context.registration from the launch on every statement; initialized on launch and completed on the course use the launch activity_id as the object when present, else course.yaml's id, with course.yaml's id in contextActivities.grouping when the two differ; module, check, interaction and fridge statements use the D24 ids with the course as contextActivities.parent; version header 1.0.2; the Authorization value verbatim. Verbs are ADL's: initialized, completed, answered, interacted. Both fridges send completed with their score when they end.
- The fridge is one component driven by its fridge file (D17): shelves, items with their shelf and reason, feedback mode (reason, or flash only), score mode (right first time out of n, or points), timer seconds or none, leaderboard entries or none, confetti or not, a Try again. Pointer drag with mouse and touch, the keyboard route (Enter picks up, arrows move between shelves, Enter places, Escape puts back), a live region that announces item, shelf and result, and a visible status line with the same words (D14). The one-shot is keyboard-operable too and its comparison row says so.
- Accessibility is WCAG 2.2 AA throughout (D14): real buttons and links, 44px targets, visible focus, every control reachable by Tab, right and wrong carried by an icon as well as colour.
- The package (D18): `npm run package` builds with relative asset paths and writes dist/agent-course.zip with tincan.xml at its root naming the course activity id and index.html as the launch file; dist/ stays gitignored.
- Dependencies are added by .2 (the YAML plugin, the schema library, @xapi/xapi, the three @fontsource packages) and .12 (a zip library) only; no other bead touches package.json.
- Review additions (epic-review, 2026-10-15), each a rule:
  - One screen type per screen. A storyboard screen that combines types becomes consecutive screens in the YAML (module 00's "Just ask" is the chat, then the tick-everything choose with the "what just happened" cards shown once checked, then the one-shot fridge; every storyboard Check screen is two choose screens, "Check 1 of 2" and "Check 2 of 2"). Acceptance counts refer to the YAML, never to the storyboard's screen numbers. Where the design and the storyboard differ in copy, the design wins; in structure, this rule wins.
  - Scene blocks are: paragraph, cards, quote, numbered list, table, two columns of blocks, a monospace block, a stats row (numbers with captions), and an aside with a glossary term. That covers the stepped plays, the timeline, the gate output, the pull request's chapters and the numbers card. Module 04's finding journey is a scene (steps 1 and 2), a choose (the verdict, with the fix revealed on the right option) and nothing else.
  - A choose option may carry reveal blocks, shown only when that option is chosen; a choose may carry after blocks, shown once checked, and an optional box panel where each option names a wall it draws when ticked (module 03). Module 04's "the fix" is a reveal on the right verdict; wrong verdicts show their feedback and Try again.
  - The chat is a scripted exchange: a fixed learner opening, agent messages, optional reply options each with the agent's scripted reply. No free-text box, no branches, no debriefs in round one; nothing in the storyboard uses them.
  - The frame gives every screen three things: its content, its saved answer when one exists (the screen renders itself answered, with the feedback shown), and a read-only view of the module's progress (every slug's latest answer and score). Screens report through one event callback: answered (slug, right, score raw and max: 1 of 1 for a check, n of 8 for the order, n of 6 for the match, one event per Check press), interacted (slug, option; one per option pick, three for the brief's defaults), fridge ended (slug, score raw and max), takeaway reached. The 07 score screen is a scene whose stats row reads the module's progress ("14 out of 14").
  - Module 07 has no checks; its end screen is its takeaway (the complete box with the ring, then the end copy). The score is 28 points: 14 checks (two in each of modules 00 to 06), the order's 8 and the walls' 6; scaled is points over 28.
  - A module is complete when its takeaway is reached. Next is disabled on a scored screen until it is answered, so reaching the takeaway means every check is done (this reconciles D11); unscored interactions can be skipped. Back always works; Back on a module's first screen and Next on its takeaway go to the home page.
  - Statements: answered is sent on every Check press of a scored screen (so a wrong-then-right check sends two); interacted once per option pick on unscored screens; each fridge play sends completed once when it ends; the course completed statement as the DECISIONS say. The storyboards' own "Statements" lines are superseded by D19 and this list: no "module launched", no chapter-opened, no per-item fridge statements.
  - A fridge play ends when every item is placed, or, on the one-shot, when the timer runs out; Try again or Reset starts a new play; leaving the screen mid-play ends nothing. The one-shot has a "No timer" control that turns the timer off before or during a play (WCAG 2.2.1); its wrong drop puts the item back and the status line and live region say only that it returned, never why. After Enter picks an item up the keyboard cursor starts on the first shelf, so the salad drawer is three arrow-downs from the top.
  - Ids: module, check, interaction and fridge statements use course.yaml's course id as contextActivities.parent and the launch activity_id as grouping when it differs; State is keyed by the launch activity_id when present, else course.yaml's id. A launch with an endpoint but no actor or auth is treated as no launch (preview). A State read that fails or returns anything but a JSON State document counts as no State. localStorage is keyed by course id and registration ("preview" when there is none), and a launched registration never loads preview's progress.
  - course.yaml carries the course's description (for tincan.xml) and the copy of the scenario page and the home page (role chip, heading, memo, lines, button; thesis quote and attribution; module blurbs), so the course-level pages are content too.
  - No router library and no drag library: hash routing and pointer drag are hand-rolled, so nothing but .2 and .12 touches package.json.
  - The gate has no integration tier (CLAUDE.md): "full gate" is lint, typecheck, unit and e2e, and `npm run package` joins `npm run gate` with a self-check of the zip it writes.
  - Tests the shell and frame commit use their own inline fixtures, never the stub modules .10, .11 and .15 replace.

**SEQUENCING**
planned=18 beads in 4 groups, sonnet=4 opus=14.
.1 alone. .2 alone: it sets the content schema every other bead reads and adds the dependencies.
.3 .10 .11 .15 together — disjoint: src/**, content/modules/0[0-3].yaml, content/modules/0[4-7].yaml, content/fridge/**.
.16 alone: it sets the screen pattern (the frame, the registry, the callback, the saved-answer and progress props).
.4 .5 .6 .8 together — disjoint: src/screens/chat and src/screens/brief; src/screens/choose; src/fridge and src/screens/fridge; src/xapi. The three screen beads wait for the frame and for the content they play; the xAPI bead waits for the frame.
.7 .17 together — disjoint: src/fridge, src/screens/fridge and src/screens/compare; src/screens/match and src/screens/order.
.9 .12 together — disjoint: src/course, src/progress, src/App.tsx and src/main.tsx; scripts/package, vite.config.ts and package.json.
.18 alone, after the progress store (same files). .13 alone, after the statements, the content and the package. Then .14, the walkthrough, last.
Hazards: src/content/** is .2's alone (the schema). src/screens/index.ts is .16's alone; the screen beads overwrite only their own folders. src/course/tracking.tsx is created by .3 and filled by .8; no later bead touches it. vite.config.ts, package.json and package-lock.json are .2's first and .12's last, in different phases.

title: An xAPI course on getting the most out of agents, built by the workflow it teaches
description:
WHAT IT IS. An xAPI course for the company's LMS (SparkLMS) that teaches how to get the most out of AI agents, built by the workflow it teaches. It opens as a scenario (you are a learning designer, a client wants a fridge activity the authoring tool cannot do, you have an agent), then eight short modules each add one wall to the box round the agent: the record, done, the gate, other agents, evidence, and the retro round it all; scripted fake-agent interactions, a check with feedback per module, a scored capstone, and both fridge activities real and playable side by side.

WHO AND WHERE. Learning designers (LED and LXD are the same role) and anyone interested at the company, on SparkLMS, alone, about 50 minutes, on a laptop or tablet; keyboard and screen reader throughout.

IN SCOPE. The engine (Vite, React, TypeScript) rendering YAML-authored modules; the eight modules' content as in docs/course/ (storyboard) and the design's first pass; the fake-agent dialogue engine; the fridge drag-and-drop component in two configurations; the xAPI layer (TinCan launch, 1.0.2, statements D19, State resume D22, preview mode with an in-memory store); the tincan.xml package build; unit tests on statements and schema, Playwright through the whole course against the in-memory store asserting every statement; the recorded walkthrough.

OUT OF SCOPE (later rounds or epics). cmi5 or SCORM packaging; the Spark postMessage bridge, keydown forwarding and the Close button (D23); narration and video (D12); a pass mark (D11) unless UAT needs "passed"; a developer track; translation.

DECISIONS. D1-D17 are the content decisions C1-C17 in docs/course/README.md §9 (same numbers): D1 audience; D2 one message, agents review better than they build; D3 outcome, six walls; D4 eight modules following the loop; D5 module shape and the box diagram; D6 the fridge activity as the worked example; D7 scripted fake agent authored as data; D8 invented examples with two real cards; D9 the workflow's own names with a glossary; D10 second person, Ross credited; D11 checks with feedback, score reported, no pass mark; D12 text and interaction only; D13 content as data in the repo; D14 WCAG 2.2 AA; D15 statements, the smallest set; D16 the course opens as a scenario; D17 the fridge activity is real, two configurations. From this brief (reasons in the notes): D18 TinCan launch, tincan.xml zip, header 1.0.2, preview mode with an in-memory store and a badge; D19 the statements (initialized, completed per module, answered per check, interacted per choice, completed on the course with completion and scaled score; no passed/failed); D20 @xapi/xapi with the fetch adapter behind a Tracker interface, a non-blocking queue with one retry; D21 one YAML file per module and for the fridges, schema-checked at build; D22 resume via the State API with a localStorage fallback, any module openable from home; D23 Spark specifics (auth verbatim, actor verbatim, launch activity_id as the course object, bridge unused); D24 activity ids under https://rosslote.github.io/agent-course/.

DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. Touch a real agent; fetch anything at run time beyond the record store it is launched with; judge free text; grade with a pass mark; name the company or any client.

Log: docs/conversations/2026-10-15-brief.md and 2026-10-15-what-the-course-teaches.md. Design: https://claude.ai/artifact/My3Z79MHvyCBktJsMfAggM, source in docs/design/2026-10-15-first-pass/.
notes:
PROBLEM
An xAPI course on the company's LMS (SparkLMS) teaching how to get the most out of agents, built by the workflow it teaches. Content settled 2026-10-15 (docs/course/, C1-C17 = D1-D17); design first pass at https://claude.ai/artifact/My3Z79MHvyCBktJsMfAggM (source in docs/design/2026-10-15-first-pass/). This brief settled implementation: launch and package, statements, library, authoring format, resume.

FOUND (2026-10-15)
- The LMS needs xAPI 1.0.2 (Ross); a later version did not work. The spec says an LRS MUST accept any version header starting with "1.0.", so a client pinned to 1.0.2 is valid against every 1.0.x LRS.
- SparkLMS launch (Ross's example URL, UAT): the classic TinCan launch. Query string: endpoint (https://<host>/xapi/), auth (the Authorization header value verbatim, scheme "tincan <token> <registration>"), actor (an account-based Agent: objectType, name, account{homePage, name}), registration (UUID), activity_id (the module's id as the LMS knows it; for an Evolve module "http://evolve/<id>"). Extra Spark-only params: keydown-message, keydown-events, enqueue-statement-message (tincan.enqueueStatement), enqueue-registration-message, close-message (close): names for a postMessage bridge to the LMS frame.
- The LRS answers with "WWW-Authenticate: tincan" and CORS open to every origin with Authorization and X-Experience-API-Version allowed, so direct browser calls work; it has no /about resource (404 with a valid token), so versions cannot be discovered and the header must simply be 1.0.2. The module's own files sit behind an authenticating CloudFront, so the Evolve module's use of the bridge could not be read.
- Library: xAPI.js (@xapi/xapi, TypeScript) takes the auth string verbatim, has a version option, XAPI.getTinCanLaunchData(), sendStatement, a fetch adapter. TinCanJS does the same, older. The State API exists in 1.0.x for per-learner resume data keyed by activity, agent and registration.

DECISIONS
D1-D17: the content decisions C1-C17 in docs/course/README.md §9, adopted with the same numbers.
D18 Launch and package: the TinCan launch; a zip with tincan.xml at the root naming the course activity id and index.html; version header 1.0.2; when no launch data is in the URL the course runs in preview mode against an in-memory record store and shows a PREVIEW badge. Reason: that is how SparkLMS launches (the example URL), and the preview keeps the gates and local runs honest.
D19 Statements: on launch "initialized" (course); per module "completed" (module activity); per check "answered" with result.response and result.success; per fake-agent choice "interacted" with the option as result.response; on finishing every module "completed" on the course with result.completion true and result.score.scaled (0-1, from the checks and the capstone); no "passed" or "failed" (D11). Every statement carries context.registration from the launch and the course as contextActivities.parent on module-level statements. Reason: the smallest set a designer can read completion, score and wandering from; "passed" is added only if UAT shows Spark needs it to mark completion.
D20 Library and sending: @xapi/xapi with the fetch adapter and version "1.0.2", wrapped in one small Tracker interface (send, setState, getState) so the in-memory store swaps in for tests and preview; statements go through a queue that never blocks the learner and retries once; failures are logged, and shown only in preview. Reason: typed, maintained, takes the Spark auth string as-is; the interface keeps the LRS out of the components.
D21 Authoring format: one YAML file per module under the content folder (screens, copy, interactions with every option and branch, checks with feedback), the fridge configurations as YAML too, all validated against a schema at build time so a bad edit fails the fast gate. Reason: designers edit prose and structured scripts together; YAML reads as text and the schema catches mistakes before a run.
D22 Resume: progress (modules completed, checks answered, capstone score) kept with the xAPI State API under the course activity, agent and registration, with localStorage as a fallback when there is no record store; the home page always lets a learner open any module. Reason: a learner leaves and comes back on the LMS; State is per registration there.
D23 Spark specifics: the auth value from the URL is sent verbatim as the Authorization header (no Basic encoding); the actor from the URL is used verbatim on every statement; course-level statements use the launch activity_id as their object when present, else tincan.xml's id, with the tincan.xml id in contextActivities.grouping when the two differ; the Spark postMessage bridge and keydown forwarding are not used in round one (direct calls work: CORS is open); close-message is a later round's "Close" button. Reason: the example URL and the LRS's CORS headers; nothing seen is unreachable by direct calls.
D24 Activity ids: course https://rosslote.github.io/agent-course/ (stable, need not resolve), modules .../modules/<nn>, checks .../modules/<nn>/checks/<n>, interactions .../modules/<nn>/interactions/<slug>, the fridges .../fridge/<one-shot|accepted>. Reason: one stable root the LMS imports from tincan.xml; the hierarchy reads in a report.

OPEN
- Verify on Spark UAT after the first import: completion shown without "passed"; the State API accepted; the activity_id the LMS passes for a tincan.xml package. Any gap becomes a bead.
- Later rounds: the Spark postMessage bridge and Close button; whether Ross's name stays on the home page quote (D10); LMS module length limits (none known).

ROUNDS
- 2026-10-15 round 1: five questions asked (launch and package, statements, library, authoring, resume) with recommendations. Ross answered with the SparkLMS launch URL and "your defaults are fine for the rest": D18-D22 as recommended, D23-D24 from the URL and the LRS's headers. Brief closed; summary in the description.
